newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran cleric says Farrakhan inspired by God.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric says Farrakhan inspired by God.

text.p: A senior Iranian cleric on Friday praised U.S. Black Moslem leader Louis Farrakhan, saying God had inspired him to unite American Moslems.

"One becomes certain that nothing but the hand of God has inspired such people to gather the Moslems in the heart of the Great Satan (United States)," judiciary head Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi said in a mass prayer sermon broadcast on Tehran radio.
"This is what the Imam (late Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini) meant by saying that our revolution would be exported," Yazdi told worshippers gathered at the Tehran University campus.

Yazdi was referring to a rally of tens of thousands of Nation of Islam supporters in New York on Wednesday, in which Farrakhan blasted the United States, saying it led the world in murder, crime and rape.
Farrakhan visited Iran in February to attend ceremonies marking the 1979 revolution that brought Khomeini to power.
The visit, part of a tour that also included Libya and Iraq, drew harsh criticism by the U.S. State Department.

Iran denies U.S. charges of sponsoring terrorism and trying to export its revolution by force, but says many Islamic movements are inspired by the revolution that deposed the late shah who was a close ally of the United States, dubbed "Great Satan" by Khomeini.
